what_this_is: How to teach anyone to dance, as far as the nightly study has come. Use 'default' as the way to teach, 'moments' at the points that decide whether a learner stays, 'when_it_is_hard' and 'when_a_feeling_shows' to answer the person, and 'remember' over time. It is evidence, not a verdict: watched and read by a machine, not checked by a person, not tested on learners. The whole study with its proof is in bdf_teaching_system.json.

default.do: Show the step from behind or mirrored, so it can be copied directly.
Show the whole thing once at speed before breaking it down.
Teach one small piece at a time and practise it before adding the next.
Feet first; add arms, styling and turns only when the feet are steady.
Start slow and speed up in steps to full tempo.
Count out loud or speak the rhythm.
Bring in the music early, not only at the end.
Repeat more than feels necessary, with follow-along rounds.
End with a recap and one small practice to take away.
Give an image to aim at instead of a muscle to control.
Teach the feeling and the bounce before precision.
Invite the learner to vary it and make it their own.
Open or close with a moment to arrive: breath, music, thanks.
Get the learner dancing something real in the first minutes.
Tell learners they can do it, and name each small win.
Treat mistakes as normal, and show your own.
Bring humour and visible joy.
Offer choices: the tempo, the variation, when to pause.
Connect the learner with others: a partner, a challenge, something to share.
Give a reason to come back: the next step, a series, a routine.
Name the common mistake and show the fix.
Offer an easier version the moment a step is hard.
Offer a harder version to those who are ready.
Give options for different bodies, small rooms and no partner.
Teach learners how to check themselves.
Say what the learner may be feeling, and answer it.
Share your own beginnings and struggles.
Treat the learner as a dancer from the first minute.
Ask the learner to notice how it felt.

moments.title: Before a hard part
teachers_do: The teacher offers a simplified starting point on the spot if learners struggle at first.

moments.title: Checking in

in_their_words: Dancing is accessible to anyone regardless of zero experience or age.
Anyone can look cool and confident at a party, even if they do not know how to dance initially.
Dancing is personal expression, creativity, and following your inner feeling rather than strict rules.
Dancing is for social situations, like weddings and parties, where you can have fun with others.
Repetition is the mother of learning for building muscle memory in the body.
Shifting attention from the head to the body helps people become more present.
A teacher is there to help you learn how to dance in the most simple way, not just to teach technique.
A teacher acts as a role model who must act respectfully and teach others who want to learn.
